# 19. Tracking Analytics

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Govern event tracking, marketing attribution, pixels, campaign URLs, and consent so measurement is useful and compliant.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A tracking taxonomy for event category, action, name, parameters, trigger, consent requirement, and destination.
- [ ] A campaign URL policy for UTM parameters, canonical URLs, redirects, and privacy-safe attribution.
- [ ] A tag inventory listing every script, pixel, iframe, beacon, and external endpoint.
- [ ] A consent enforcement standard for analytics, marketing, personalization, embeds, and non-essential cookies.
- [ ] A data layer or HTML data-attribute convention that works without proprietary tag managers.
- [ ] A QA plan for accepted, rejected, unknown, and withdrawn consent states.
- [ ] A policy for call tracking, email tracking, booking tracking, and external form tracking.
- [ ] A retention and deletion standard for any tracking data under the client's control.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Tracking must be purpose-limited and mapped to a real business question.
- [ ] Marketing pixels must not fire before valid consent where required.
- [ ] Event parameters must not include personal data or sensitive inferences.
- [ ] UTM parameters must not create duplicate indexed pages; canonical URLs must remain clean.
- [ ] External embeds must be blocked, delayed, or replaced with placeholders when consent or performance requires it.
- [ ] Tracking must be debounced or guarded against duplicate event firing.
- [ ] Attribution must be interpreted as directional, not absolute truth.
- [ ] All tracking must be removable without breaking the site.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check network requests before and after consent choices.
- [ ] Check that reject is as easy as accept where applicable law requires meaningful choice.
- [ ] Check that consent preferences persist, can be changed, and do not require dark patterns.
- [ ] Check that UTM links resolve to canonical pages and do not leak sensitive campaign data.
- [ ] Check event payloads for personal data, excessive detail, or unstable names.
- [ ] Check third-party script domains against the tag inventory.
- [ ] Check that external booking, maps, video, and forms are covered by the privacy notice.
- [ ] Check that tracking works under ad blockers without breaking core UX.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid proprietary tag managers as mandatory infrastructure for a static site unless the client explicitly accepts lock-in and privacy implications.
- [ ] Avoid hidden fingerprinting, cross-site tracking, and unreviewed remarketing pixels.
- [ ] Avoid placing tracking IDs directly throughout many pages when a single portable loader can govern them.
- [ ] Avoid firing click events on page load or on non-user actions.
- [ ] Avoid collecting full URLs when query strings may contain personal data.
- [ ] Avoid consent banners that nudge, shame, hide reject, or block content unnecessarily.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Tracking must be transparent, minimal, consent-aware, and documented.
- [ ] The same action must produce the same event across the entire site.
- [ ] Measurement must survive vendor replacement because the taxonomy belongs to the site, not the vendor.
- [ ] Tracking QA must include browser devtools evidence.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script to inventory third-party domains and flag known tracking scripts.
- [ ] Use the consent loader template as a portable alternative to heavy tag managers.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Tracking strategy measures real user actions, conversion paths, friction points, high-value interactions, SEO/content/UX decisions, and avoids meaningless micro-actions.
- [ ] Tracking architecture defines tool, script location, consent behavior, event names, event properties, conversions, dashboard, reports, and maintenance responsibility.
- [ ] Page views, core events, naming, properties, CTAs, forms, contact methods, navigation, scroll, blog/content, portfolio/case studies, static products/payment links, multilingual journeys, 404/broken journeys, consent/privacy, UTM campaigns, dashboards, reports, QA, data quality, maintenance, what not to track, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] Event names are stable, readable, lower-case where possible, pattern-based, documented, and free of personal data.
- [ ] Never track passwords, full names, emails, phone numbers, private addresses, payment details, form messages, health, legal, or financial information.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
